say.text: PDA is the familiar extra shunt, so it feels like the fifth. ASD and PDA may both accompany TOF, but pentalogy names the ASD.
TOF already has a large VSD, so another can seem the next addition. Pentalogy of Fallot is TOF plus an ASD.
Yes. PYQs expected pentalogy of Fallot = TOF + ASD; CDC confirms and calls it an old term seldom used now.
Pentalogy is five in all: the four plus one septal defect, but not in the ventricle.
Drill 8. Pentalogy of Fallot is TOF plus:
Loud murmur plus a TOF label suggests a crisis. But in a tet spell the murmur decreases in intensity, and a spell is not a pink child.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so keep this: RVOT resistance below systemic resistance gives a pink Tet.

say.text: Yes. Infants with moderate RVOT obstruction may be asymptomatic apart from a loud murmur; these are 'pink Tets'. RVOT resistance below systemic resistance means minimal or no cyanosis.
'Blue baby' is the textbook picture, so a pink one seems to contradict TOF. But if RVOT resistance is less than systemic vascular resistance, the patient is minimally cyanotic or acyanotic.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so keep this: RVOT resistance below systemic resistance gives a pink Tet.

say.text: Compare resistance across the RVOT with systemic resistance. Which is lower?
Drill 9. A 2-month-old, not diagnosed before birth, is pink and feeding well, with a loud harsh systolic murmur at the left upper sternal border. Echo shows TOF. Best explanation?

choices.label: The loud murmur means he is in a spell
The echo is wrong; TOF is always cyanotic from birth

say.text: Down syndrome is the best-known syndrome in congenital heart disease, so it tempts. For TOF, the most common syndromic association is the 22q11.2 deletion.
Turner syndrome is another named heart-linked syndrome. The source names the 22q11.2 deletion as the most common syndromic association of TOF.
Yes. The 22q11.2 deletion is the most common syndromic association of TOF.
Drill 10. The most common syndromic association of TOF is:
'Most common association' can sound like 'most cases'. Sources differ: up to 15% of TOF cases versus 6% in one TOF cohort.
Yes. Sources differ on frequency: up to 15% of TOF cases, versus 6% in one TOF cohort. Quote the spread if asked.
A deletion this well known can seem near-universal. Most common is not nearly all: figures are up to 15% and 6%.

The two ranges are close, so swapping them is easy. StatPearls gives 5 to 7 per 10,000 and Garagiola and Thorne 3–5.
Prevalence figures are easy to scale wrongly. StatPearls gives 5 to 7 per 10,000 live births and a prevalence of 1 in 3,000 births; the sources differ.
Yes. StatPearls gives 5 to 7 per 10,000 live births, Garagiola and Thorne 3–5, and Gagliardi et al. about 3 to 6.

Drill 18. Without surgery, deaths from hypoxic spells, stroke and brain abscess are roughly:
A brain abscess is a classic cyanotic-heart complication, so it tempts. It accounts for 13%; the most frequent cause is hypoxic spells at 68%.
Stroke is another recognised complication, so it feels likely. It accounts for 17%; hypoxic spells lead at 68%.
Yes. The most frequent causes of mortality without surgical intervention include hypoxic spells (68%).
Drill 19. The most frequent cause of death in unrepaired TOF is:
A loud P2 goes with raised pulmonary pressure, so it is tempting. In TOF, with significant RVOT obstruction, most blood bypasses the pulmonary bed, and P2 is usually inaudible.
Yes. The pulmonic component of S2 is usually inaudible.
Splitting is how S2 is usually described in right-sided disease, so this tempts. In TOF the pulmonic component is usually inaudible.

choices.label: Loud, because of raised pulmonary pressure

say.text: A shunt suggests more lung flow, so plethora is tempting. With significant RVOT obstruction, most blood shunts toward the aorta, bypassing the lungs.
The film can therefore show decreased pulmonary vascular markings.
Yes. With significant RVOT obstruction most blood bypasses the pulmonary bed, so films can show pulmonary oligaemia.
Right ventricular load suggests a big heart. StatPearls describes a normal-size heart silhouette with an upturned apex.
Drill 21. What do the lung fields show on a TOF chest X-ray?
CT gives crisp anatomy, so it feels like the standard. The gold standard for diagnosis is the echocardiogram.
MRI is detailed and radiation-free, so first-line seems plausible. The primary modality for diagnosis is echocardiography.
Yes. Echocardiography is the gold standard and the primary diagnostic modality.
Drill 22. The gold standard investigation for diagnosing TOF is:
ASD is common, so it feels like a member. The four are VSD, overriding aorta, RVOT obstruction, RVH; ASD and PDA may accompany TOF.
PDA is the other accompanying lesion, so it is tempting. Pentalogy of Fallot is TOF plus an atrial septal defect.
Yes. ASD and PDA may accompany TOF, outside the four. Pentalogy is TOF plus ASD, an old term seldom used now.

choices.label: An ASD is one of the four classic components of TOF
Pentalogy is TOF plus a PDA, and ASD plays no part
An ASD may accompany TOF; TOF plus ASD is the old pentalogy
